author.name: Model Monica

challenge.name: The Warehouse Flood
challenge.description: A forecast job failed silently for three days, leaving stores ordering blind, and the team never knew until the warehouse was flooded with unsold promotion stock. #reliability_ruth# argues that the performance monitoring must be automated and governed to catch such failures instantly, while #efficiency_emilia# is willing to accept a manual monthly audit of the logs to save on tooling costs.

output.content: I need the retraining trigger to be fully automated. Right now, we rely on manual checks to decide when the model updates, which leaves a dangerous gap where drift can quietly degrade our forecast accuracy. I want the system to detect shifts in demand patterns and kick off retraining on its own, without waiting for a human to notice the drop in performance. The more frequently the model adapts to new data, the better our predictions stay. I am not asking for a fixed weekly schedule; I am asking for a continuous, automated loop that reacts to the data as it arrives. This ensures the forecast remains sharp and reliable, reducing the risk of bad order suggestions reaching the store managers.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly states that 'the more frequently the model adapts to new data, the better our predictions stay,' indicating that exceeding the minimum requirement of a continuous loop (e.g., via higher frequency or more sensitive triggers) would make the stakeholder happier.
